question: What time does my flight to Tokyo depart and from which gate?

sessions.content: Just booked my trip! My flight to Tokyo departs at 7:30 AM from gate B12.
Noted — Tokyo flight at 7:30 AM from gate B12. An early start, so plan to be at the airport well before dawn.
The airline changed my flight to Tokyo — it now departs at 10:45 AM from gate C3. Ignore the old 7:30 AM gate B12 details.
Updated — Tokyo flight is now 10:45 AM from gate C3. The later departure should make the morning much easier.

question: Where do I keep my router admin password?
answer: in the black notebook on my desk

sessions.content: I always write my router admin password in the black notebook on my desk — never in a password manager.
A paper copy in the black notebook works, as long as the desk stays private. Maybe note a hint to the notebook rather than the password itself.
It also has the wifi SSID and the guest password on the same page.
Good — one page for all the network details makes recovery painless if the router ever needs a reset.

question: I just finished Piranesi and I would give it a four.
answer: Piranesi — 4/5 — a quiet, labyrinthine mystery set in an endless house of statues and tides.

sessions.content: New rule for our chats: whenever I mention a book I finished, I will give it a rating out of five. Reply with the title, the rating, and a one-line note.
Got it — title, rating out of five, and a one-line note for every book you finish. Ready for the first one.
I finished The Left Hand of Darkness and I would give it a five.
The Left Hand of Darkness — 5/5 — a masterpiece of anthropology disguised as science fiction.

question: Summarize the full arc of my kitchen renovation from demo day to the last milestone.
answer: demo week with parents, garage temporary sink, cabinets in at three weeks, quartz counters two more weeks, then backsplash tile and farmhouse sink to finish

sessions.content: We finally started the kitchen renovation. Demo day is Monday and the cabinets arrive in three weeks.
Demo to cabinets in three weeks is a tight but doable schedule. Are you living at home through it?
We are staying with my parents for the demo week, then back home with a temporary sink in the garage.
A garage temporary sink is a classic renovation survival move. The parents week covers the worst of the dust.
The cabinets are in! The counters still need two weeks for the quartz to be cut.
Cabinets in means the room finally looks like a kitchen again. What is the last big milestone after the quartz?
Just the backsplash tile and the farmhouse sink hookup, then we are done.
So close to the finish line — after the quartz it is just backsplash and sink, and you get the kitchen back.
